html:
Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus was a Byzantine emperor of the Macedonian dynasty, in name from 913 to 959. He is best known as a scholar whose books are a main source for the 900s.

"Born in the purple", he became emperor as a boy. His mother Zoe ruled for him, and then the admiral Romanos Lekapenos took power as senior emperor until 944. Constantine spent those years on learning, and ruled alone only from 945.

He had scholars gather excerpts from older writers, and wrote or directed the Book of Ceremonies and De Administrando Imperio, advice to his son that is a key source on the Pechenegs, the Rus and Slav lands such as Zachlumia and the Severians. This revival, seen in works like the Paris Psalter, is called the Macedonian Renaissance. His excerpts later fed the Suda.
